candidates.summary: "Map iteration order is unspecified" is a Go fact; GnoVM ranges maps in insertion order and docs.gno.land says so
candidates.failure_scenario: A newcomer or agent reads AGENTS.md:49-50 as the authoritative Gno-vs-Go list and carries away that gno map iteration is unordered. GnoVM's MapValue is a doubly-linked MapList plus an index map (gnovm/pkg/gnolang/values.go:935-1016), so `range` walks insertion order, stable within a run and across the amino round-trip; docs/resources/gno-data-structures.md:132 states it outright: map iteration order follows insertion order, unlike Go. The rule the line draws (don't build Render output from a map) survives for the reason that doc gives next (do not rely on it for correctness or public Render output), but the reason printed here is the opposite of what the VM does, in the one file the repo offers as its Gno-vs-Go reference.
candidates.verify_by: tests/b1-claims-gno-semantics_test.gno, TestMapIterationOrderIsDeterministic: insert z,a,m,b,q,c,y,d and range twice; expect a varying or non-insertion order per AGENTS.md, observe "zambqcyd" both times. Cross-check docs/resources/gno-data-structures.md:132 in gnolang/gno.
candidates.evidence: gno test -v . -> MAPORDER="zambqcyd" (insertion order, not unspecified); --- PASS: TestMapIterationOrderIsDeterministic. gnolang/gno docs/resources/gno-data-structures.md:132: "In Gno, map iteration order follows insertion order, unlike Go which uses randomized iteration order".

candidates.summary: "a green local run means a green CI" ignores the toolchain both sides rebuild independently
candidates.failure_scenario: CI installs gno from gnolang/gno master at job time (.github/workflows/ci.yml:29-34) under `go-version: stable`, while the Makefile's GNO defaults to whatever `gno` the contributor installed, possibly months of master ago. Targets cannot drift; toolchains do, on two unpinned axes, and the review round itself shows the gap: the PR body reports verification on gno master.184+393b6f92a, this round built master bbd9b2ffe. A contributor whose local run is green then sees CI red on a VM or lint change nobody in this repo made, and the line tells them that cannot happen.
candidates.verify_by: read .github/workflows/ci.yml:29-34 (unpinned master, go-version: stable) against Makefile:3 `GNO ?= gno`; confirm no pin exists on either side.
candidates.evidence: ci.yml installs via install.sh from refs master with --from-source, no sha or tag; Makefile:3 is `GNO ?= gno`. No version is pinned anywhere in the repo.

candidates.summary: `dev` hardcodes gnodev while test, lint and fmt honour $(GNO)
candidates.failure_scenario: The PR adds `GNO ?= gno` so a contributor can point the repo at a toolchain that is not on PATH, and test, lint and fmt use it. dev still runs bare `gnodev`, so that same contributor runs three of the four documented commands and `make dev` fails with command not found, which is the one command README step 3 and AGENTS.md's Commands block put in front of a newcomer first.
candidates.verify_by: grep -n 'GNO\|gnodev' Makefile; then `make dev GNO=/path/to/gno` with gnodev off PATH.
candidates.evidence: Makefile:3 GNO ?= gno; :19 `gnodev .`; :22 :25 :28 all `$(GNO) ...`. gnodev is a separate binary (contribs/gnodev), so GNO cannot cover it; a GNODEV ?= gnodev is the symmetric fix.

candidates.summary: the help awk uses `.*?`, which is not POSIX ERE, on the target AGENTS.md makes the entry point
candidates.failure_scenario: AGENTS.md:15 and the README both tell the reader `make` lists every target, and .DEFAULT_GOAL makes it the first thing anyone runs. The recipe's FS and match pattern both use the PCRE lazy quantifier `.*?`, which POSIX ERE does not define; on a machine whose /usr/bin/awk is not gawk (mawk on Debian and Ubuntu, busybox awk in a container) the behaviour is the implementation's, and a first-run `make` that errors or prints nothing is the worst possible first impression for this repo. Verified green under gawk 5.4.1 only; mawk is not installed on this machine.
candidates.verify_by: run `mawk 'BEGIN{FS=":.*?## "} /^[a-zA-Z_-]+:.*?## /{printf "  %-8s %s\n",$1,$2}' Makefile` and `busybox awk` with the same script; compare against the gawk output.
candidates.evidence: make -C <worktree> under gawk 5.4.1 prints all six targets correctly. mawk and busybox are absent here (`which mawk busybox` -> not found), so the non-gawk half is unrun.
